sections.heading: Overview
content: Humana adjudicates a claim for services provided to a plan member based on the information submitted in that claim and information related to that claim. If a qualified healthcare provider disagrees with Humana’s adjudication of that claim, based on the information submitted in that claim, that provider may submit to Humana a request for a dispute review of the plan’s determination. If a provider submits a request for a dispute review timely and with all required information, Humana will review the claim to determine whether to revise the adjudication. Humana plans may use medical records and other available relevant documentation to review a dispute . This policy establishes the applicable timeframe for a qualified healthcare provider submission of a dispute request. Note : A corrected claim is a provider’s submission of information that constitutes a material change to an existing claim. A claim submission that constitutes a material change to an existing claim is not a disagreement about Humana’s adjudication of the claim as based on the information in the previous claim submission. Therefore, Humana plans will not review a corrected claim as a dispute .

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. A qualified healthcare provider may contest the payment, denial or nonpayment of a claim in writing with at least the following information: • Member name and identification number • Date of service • Relationship of the subscriber to the patient • Claim number • Name, National Provider Identifier (NPI) and tax identification number of the provider of the services • Charge amount • Payment amount • Proposed correct payment amount • Difference between the amount paid and the proposed correct payment amount • Brief explanation of the basis for the contestation request • Relevant supporting documentation, such as, medical records, invoice, or referral form Note: Information about the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) administrative appeal processes is available at Humana.com/Appeals .

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Specific Requirements
content: Unless otherwise stated in the contract, an in-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 18 months from the receipt of the original claim determination. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 180 days from the receipt of the original claim determination. Multiple provider dispute requests per provider encounter are generally unacceptable. It is necessary, therefore, in a provider dispute request after an initial dispute determination, to explicitly identify specific new material information that justifies further review.

sections.heading: Medicaid Specific Requirements
content: Unless otherwise stated in the contract, an in-network qualified healthcare provider may submit a dispute request within 18 months from the receipt of the original claim determination. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider does not have a contractual relationship with a particular plan that would afford that qualified healthcare provider direct rights against that plan. An out-of-network qualified healthcare provider lacks, for example, the right to submit a claim, the right to require the plan to process a claim seeking a member’s plan or policy benefits, the right to submit a dispute request and the right to submit corrected claims . Those examples are not exhaustive. Without waiving any provisions that prohibit an out-of-network qualified healthcare provider from assuming an enrollee’s direct rights against the plan, a plan will allow an out-of-network qualified healthcare provider to submit a dispute request within: • The timeframe established by state or federal laws, or • 180 days from the receipt of the original claim determination when the applicable state and federal laws are silent.

sections.heading: Additional Resources on this Topic
content: Humana’s Making it Easier web-based training series includes a video on Humana’s processes for medical claim disputes and corrected claims that may supplement your understanding of this policy.

sections.heading: Definitions of Italicized Terms
content: • Corrected claim: A claim that replaces a previously submitted claim and includes material information that differs from information included in the previously submitted claim. For this purpose, "material information" is information that, because it differs from information included in the previously submitted claim, could cause some change in reimbursement if that information were considered. • Dispute: A disagreement about a previous claim determination that does not entail a change to the material information submitted for that claim. The dispute must be presented in writing, challenging the potentially adverse determination of the claim based on the previously submitted information. Medical notes, industry standards and/or Original Medicare guidelines may be used to support a dispute request. • Qualified healthcare provider: A provider who is licensed by the appropriate state agency to diagnose or treat a sickness or bodily injury and provide preventive services.

sections.heading: General Humana Resources
content: • Availity – Providers can register for access to information on a variety of topics such as eligibility, benefits, referrals, authorizations, claims and electronic remittances. • Claims processing edit notifications – Alerts of upcoming claims payment changes are posted on the first Friday of each month. • Claims resources – Providers can find information on referrals, authorizations, electronic claim submissions and more. • Making it easier – This page contains an educational series for providers and healthcare professionals. • Medical and pharmacy coverage policies – Humana publishes determinations of coverage of medical procedures, devices and medications for the treatment of various conditions. There may be variances in coverage among plans. • Publications – This page can help you find our quarterly newsletter, provider manual and other resources to help you do business with us.
